correctness.rationale: An arbitrary three-point metric always has nearest-neighbor-distance multiset (a,a,b). Distant deviations cannot help. For small deviations the cost is h+(d-h)/(1+Oprime). If the agent starts as the far member, Oprime<=2(b/a)^alpha(1+h/b)^alpha and the cubic scalar inequality settles incentives. If it starts as a close member, the low-b case is monotone, the high-b closest-pair case has a nonnegative derivative bounded below by (1-z)(2-z), and a transition to the far member has an explicit positive polynomial rational certificate at alpha=3, with monotonic reduction to lower powers. For alpha>3, a line deviation at (0,1,2) has negative initial cost derivative 2(3-alpha)/9. The embedded checker proves the polynomial identity exactly and executes 196,608 exact-rational finite checks; no extrapolation from finite tests is needed.

value.rationale: The minimal nontrivial two-facility strategic location game obtains an exact sharp admissible exponent threshold on every metric space. Truthfulness at the critical cubic power is structurally nontrivial and improves the known worst-case expected social-cost factor for this family from approximately 1.11237244 for quadratic power to approximately 1.06527445. The improvement is meaningful because the welfare factor is not sufficient for incentive compatibility. The earlier welfare formula is explicitly treated as context, not a new result.
